messages:
Nadia (People Ops): Hey team — quick question. Aisha is considering 6 weeks of voluntary unpaid leave starting June because of family reasons. With the hiring freeze still in place, she asked how unpaid leave affects PTO accrual, carryover, and benefits eligibility. Any high-level guidance we can give her before formal request?
Aisha (Eng): thanks Nadia — wanted to flag early so managers can plan coverage. Also curious if unpaid leave pauses accrual or reduces annual carryover cap.
Marcus (Eng Manager): fwiw I can cover some sprint tasks but well need to backfill for support. Curious on approvals flow too — do I approve in Lattice or just note it?
Leah (People Ops): short answer: unpaid leave typically pauses PTO accrual while on unpaid status. Carryover rules depend on duration and whether leave crosses calendar year. We should check payroll for exact proration rules.
Hannah (Payroll): @Leah correct — once pay is unpaid for a full pay period, accrual stops. If leave spans year boundary, accrual for that year is prorated; carryover caps still apply unless LOA exception granted. We can run a quick example if you want.
Nadia (People Ops): yes please — example would help Aisha decide. Also any impact to benefits continuation or COBRA triggers?
Hannah (Payroll): short bullets: 1) Benefits: if unpaid leave results in loss of active status you might need COBRA for medical; but for a 6-week unpaid leave within a 12-month period we usually maintain benefits if the employee opts to continue and pays employee portion. 2) Retirement: employer match may pause during unpaid periods. 3) PTO accrual: paused.
Sam (Finance): budget note — unpaid leave lowers headcount burn but also pauses accrual liability. If manager expects >4 weeks coverage, please open a temp contractor request via Jira.
Marcus (Eng Manager): thanks. For approvals: Ill ask Aisha to submit a formal LOA/unpaid leave request in Lattice, tag me, and cc People Ops. That work for payroll?
Hannah (Payroll): perfect. Once submitted we need start/end dates and last paid period. Payroll will calculate prorated accrual and what, if any, carryover will be impacted. Expect a confirmation within 3 business days.
Leah (People Ops): also note option: if Aisha wants to keep accruing PTO, she can opt to take unpaid leave as paid time off first (use available PTO bank) — or mix paid + unpaid. We can outline scenarios in the approval email.
Aisha (Eng): helpful — thanks. Can People Ops send a short template email I can use when filing in Lattice? Keeps it tidy.
Nadia (People Ops): will do — sending template in thread in a minute. PeopleOpsBot: Reminder: LOA/unpaid-leave form link -> https://redwood.intra/leave-form :thumbsup:
Nadia (People Ops): TEMPLATE (copy):
---
Subject: Unpaid leave request — Aisha Patel — Jun 2 to Jul 14
Hi @Marcus and People Ops,
Id like to request unpaid leave from 2025-06-02 through 2025-07-14. I have X hours of PTO and would like to apply Y days to cover first week. Please confirm payroll proration and benefits continuation.
Thanks,
Aisha
---
Nadia (People Ops): tagging @Hannah and @Sam for payroll/budget follow-up once Aisha files. Anything else we should add?
Sam (Finance): please include whether coverage will require overtime or contractor; that affects the approval.
Marcus (Eng Manager): Ill coordinate coverage plan and include a short runbook for oncall.
Leah (People Ops): ok — next steps: 1) Aisha files in Lattice using template, 2) Payroll calculates accrual/benefits impact, 3) Manager approves and confirms coverage, 4) People Ops issues confirmation email with carryover/accrual summary.
Aisha (Eng): filing now, thanks all :heart:
Hannah (Payroll): received — Ill run numbers and post back here within 2 business days with exact accrual proration and whether any carryover cap is affected.
Nadia (People Ops): thanks everyone. Marking this thread resolved for now; will leave updates here.
